rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.requirement: Housing providers receiving DND funding or with income restricted units under BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy must not impose blanket denials based on arrests or convictions and must consider applicants on a case-by-case basis. Arrests without conviction, juvenile records, convictions subject to judicial relief, and convictions older than 5 years generally cannot be considered unless there is a direct relationship to housing safety risk.
rules.summary_plain: If you apply for housing funded or regulated by Boston's DND or BPDA, they cannot automatically deny you because of arrests or old convictions. They must look at your case individually.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si solicita vivienda financiada o regulada por DND o BPDA de Boston, no pueden negarle automáticamente por arrestos o condenas antiguas. Deben evaluar su caso individualmente.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development funding and/or land, or with income restricted units created under Boston Planning and Development Agency Inclusionary Development Policy.
rules.exemptions_text: Does not apply where federal or state law imposes conflicting criminal history requirements; also does not apply to current criminal behavior or where there is a direct relationship between conviction and housing safety risk.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy, Department of Neighborhood Development, February 2017
rules.quoted_span: Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or that have income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy will not impose a blanket policy that denies housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions. Housing providers will consider applicants on a case-by-case basis.
